No propositions came through with your message, so I can't pick among them. If I had to name the strongest general refutation, it would be that the calculus needs pleasures and pains to be measurable on a single cardinal scale and comparable across persons, and no such scale exists. Without it, the "sum" of happiness is undefined, and the calculus can't guide action even in principle. Paste the options and I'll say which one matches.
